title: QuickLine telecom integration call capture
content:
Call: QuickLine (edge team) — 2024-11-05 10:00 PST
Attendees: QuickLine: Priya (eng lead), Omar (edge infra), Sam (product) | Redwood: Aisha (SE), Marco (infra), Jae (privacy)
Purpose: Scope integration for voice IVR augmentation + post-call summarization; understand latency envelope and security constraints for a small pilot (NY metro).

High level notes / constraints (raw):
- Business: need summaries + intent extraction for 20k calls/month initially; goal 250 concurrent calls at peak.
- Latency SLO: 95th p95 total round-trip < 120ms for token generation portion (they measure from RTP capture -> model token stream).
- Audio pipeline: external STT provider (real-time transcripts) -> Redwood API -> downstream analytics. STT latency adds ~60-80ms currently. We must keep inference portion ~40ms p95.
- Session pattern: many short utterances (<= 30 tokens), occasional long sequences when agents read long scripts (spikes up to 800 tokens).
- Security: customer requires VPC peering for private deployment and HSM-backed keys for any PII retention. Air-gapped on-prem possibility discussed but cost-prohibitive for pilot.
- Regulatory: some calls flagged for recording retention rules (regional), ask for SOC2 + HIPAA posture doc (Jae to share Redwood brief).

Technical gotchas / risks observed on call (notes to self):
- KV cache warmup: with short repeated prompts, prefix caching helps a lot, but their session reuse patterns are irregular; need to instrument cache hit rate by correlation id.
- Sequence length spike -> kernel path flip: For spikes to 800 tokens, runtime may switch kernels and latency jumps; propose a model variant that pins max-length or uses dynamic routing to a lower-cost long-context instance.
- Batching tradeoff: to meet 40ms token latency we probably must keep batch target small (1-4) and use low batching delay; but this raises per-token cost. Offer burst autoscale + reserved capacity for peak windows.
- SIP jitter and variable RTT from edge gateways: can see bursts where many simultaneous reconnects flood requests; recommend a small per-customer concurrency throttle + queueing policy at ingress.
- Quantization compatibility: QuickLine is cost-sensitive. Evaluate int8 vs int4 on candidate model (redwood-chat-medium?). Some early quantized builds introduce slight quality regressions on intent extraction — must include eval set.

Concrete asks from QuickLine (they will provide):
- 2 days of representative transcripts (redacted) + 1 week of anonymized session traces (timestamps, correlation ids)
- Target traffic profile: hourly qps distribution, expected concurrency windows, percent of long-session spikes
- Compliance contacts and legal POC for data retention discussion (for pilot opt-in)

Immediate proposed architecture for pilot (sketch):
- STT -> edge preprocessor (dedupe, normalize) -> private Redwood endpoint (VPC peered) with dedicated pool (reserved 2x baseline concurrency) -> streaming responses back to aggregator -> post-processing/storage in customer's analytics cluster (no PII stored by Redwood by default)
- Caching: prefix/KV cache enabled per-session id, eviction TTL tuned to session length (~5m), telemetry to expose hit/miss to QuickLine dashboard.
- Fallbacks: primary model = redwood-conversational-m (quantized int8), fallback = redwood-small-1 (lower cost) if queueing latency > 200ms or GPU capacity contention detected.

Open questions / follow-ups (for next sync):
- Priya: can QuickLine accept "sampled" transcripts rather than full call capture for pilot? (privacy/legal)
- Omar: what edge ingress behavior (SIP proxies) details — will they provide pcap or logs? We need jitter distribution.
- Sam: define exact acceptance metric for summaries (ROUGE-type? human eval?) — propose a small eval set and 3-point rubric.
- Internal: need to validate redwood-conversational-m quantized perf on A100 vs T4 (Marco to run microbench).

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Aisha: draft pilot scope doc + checklist, send to QuickLine by 2024-11-08.
- Marco: perf run (quantized redwood-conversational-m) on A100/T4, include p95 latency and throughput numbers; due 2024-11-14.
- Jae: compile Redwood compliance brief (SOC2/HIPAA summary + how KMS/HSM would map); due 2024-11-10.
- Priya (QuickLine): share 48h redacted transcripts + session traces; target 2024-11-12.
- Omar (QuickLine): share edge logs or pcap sample; target 2024-11-13.
- Marco + Aisha: prototype KV cache telemetry (simple hit/miss per session metric) and wire to demo dashboard; initial spike: 2024-11-20.

Notes-to-self (unpolished):
- Consider recommending small LRU for KV cache keys to avoid unbounded memory if customer accidentally sends full audio as a prompt.
- Could use a short-lived model variant pinned to 512 tokens for cheap fast-path; route long requests to long-context fleet. Add routing policy to rollout doc.
- If they insist on sub-40ms inference, likely need model distillation or local edge variant — flag as expensive / long lead.

Meeting follow-up plan:
- Send pilot scope + checklist (Aisha) 
- Internal sync with infra (Marco) to confirm reserved capacity pricing and burst plan
- Plan a 60m technical deep-dive with QuickLine engs (post-checklist) to review telemetry hooks and acceptance eval

Random snippets overheard (useful):
- "We have a maintenance window every night at 02:00 local—avoid heavy migrations then."
- "Our agent scripts frequently paste in long legal disclaimers -> causes long sequences and sometimes hallucinations in summaries."

End of notes.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-05: initial capture (Aisha)
- 2024-11-07: added perf asks + quantization note (Marco)
- 2024-11-12: updated with QuickLine timeline and action item ownership
